newsitem.title: NORWAY: Statoil sees 97 oil output at 488 mln bb.
newsitem.headline: Statoil sees 97 oil output at 488 mln bb.

text.p: Oilfields operated by Den norske stats oljeselskap ASA on the Norwegian continental shelf are expected to produce 488 million barrels of crude in 1997, the state oil company said.
The forecast represents a rise of 13 million barrels, or three percent, from 1996, the company's Status Weekly newsletter said.
Statoil attributed the rise to the startup of the Norne field in the Norwegian Sea in July. The development is forecast to yield 32 million barrels up to the end of 1997.
Statoil also plans to increase production from the Heidrun field off mid-Norway by roughly 12 million barrels to 88 million barrels.

The company said production at the North Sea Yme development would rise by five million barrels from last year to around 13.5 million barrels, while the Statfjord satellites are set to increase output by four million barrels to 46 million barrels.

Oil production at the main Statfjord field is forecast to decline by roughly 32 million barrels to 131 million, Statoil said. It said Gullfaks output should fall by about eight million barrels to 152 million barrels.
Statoil said it expected production at the Veslefrikk field to remain unchanged from 1996 at just over 26 million barrels.
